relatedSnapshot.title: Campaign stops after contacting 22 of 2000 scraped leads
relatedSnapshot.description:
Customer reports that after using the AI lead scraper in Acquisity to add \~2000 leads to a campaign, only 22 leads were actually contacted and the campaign shows as completed.

Details shared so far:

* All \~2000 leads appear in the campaign in Acquisity.
* Only 22 of the leads were contacted.
* The campaign is marked as completed after sending to just those 22 leads.
* Leads were expected to transfer to / be contacted via Company One, but remained in Acquisity instead.

relatedSnapshot.title: Cold Email Agent lead tools leave customer outreach blocked
relatedSnapshot.description:
Customer’s outreach remains effectively frozen due to limitations and unresolved behavior in the Cold Email Agent lead workflow, even after previous issues (ENG-3326, ENG-3838, ENG-4232, ENG-4639) were marked resolved.

Key points from the conversation:

* Customer cannot practically proceed with campaigns because there is no way to efficiently clean and segment a 4,560-lead healthcare list where only \~40–42% of leads match their ICP.
* Existing guidance to "upload leads and create different campaigns" does not address the underlying need to filter, segment, and export leads at scale from a single campaign.
* Customer reports that their outreach has been "frozen" for weeks and they are unable to move forward with both their own and client campaigns as a result.
* Customer explicitly asks what can be done to fix this and whether this is what they should expect going forward.

This ticket is to reassess the current behavior and previous resolutions for this account and ensure there is a workable, reliable path for the customer to run campaigns using large lead lists without being blocked by tooling gaps or edge-case behavior.

relatedSnapshot.title: Add lead export, filtering, and segments to Cold Email Agent
relatedSnapshot.description:
### Problem

Lead management inside the Cold Email Agent is too limited for larger campaigns. In a recent healthcare campaign with 4,560 imported leads (\~50.7K available in pool), the user had to manually review all leads and found that only \~40–42% matched their ICP, but there was no way to efficiently clean or organize the list inside the product. There is no CSV export, filtering is too basic for complex criteria, and there is no way to segment leads or tag them by quality.

### User Story

As an agency user running multi-thousand-lead campaigns, I want robust lead export, filtering, and segmentation tools so that I can clean, organize, and target my lists efficiently without spending 15–25 hours per campaign on manual cleanup or having to move data to other platforms.

### Functional Requirements

- [ ] Allow exporting campaign leads to CSV (all leads or filtered subset), including core fields like name, email, company, title, location, LinkedIn, and status.
- [ ] Add an advanced filter builder that supports multiple conditions with AND/OR logic, bulk keyword input (e.g. exclude many company keywords at once), and combining filters across fields (e.g. company + industry + title).
- [ ] Enable saving and reusing filter configurations (saved views) within a campaign.
- [ ] Support lead segments or lists within a campaign (e.g. "Strong ICP", "Borderline", "Non-ICP") that can be populated via filters or bulk actions.
- [ ] Add basic tagging for leads (e.g. "Strong Match", "Needs Review") that can be used in filters and bulk actions.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] User can export the full lead list or a filtered subset from the Leads tab to CSV and open it in a spreadsheet tool.
- [ ] User can define complex filters (including multiple "does not contain" keywords at once) and apply them without losing them on page reload.
- [ ] User can save a filter configuration, reapply it later in the same or another session, and switch quickly between saved views.
- [ ] User can create named lead segments and move leads into them using filters or selection; metrics and sending can target only a chosen segment.
- [ ] User can add and remove tags on individual or bulk-selected leads and filter by those tags when preparing a campaign.

### Out of Scope

* Changes to lead scraping logic or data sources.
* Changes to billing/credit usage; this request focuses on managing leads after they are in the platform.

relatedSnapshot.title: Opening a person in Conversations stays fast with years of history
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Opening a person in Conversations, and the record Activity tab, stay under half a second even for people with hundreds of imported calls, texts and emails. The newest items load first and older ones load as you scroll.

## Problem

Opening one person reads their history, which is cheap today (20 to 60 ms after ENG-14300). But the timeline may still build workspace-wide call tables and match texts through a rule that can't use an index, so it could slow down as 1.4M imported texts land. It also loads a person's whole history at once.

## User experience

A rep opens a person with two years of Close history: the latest 50 items appear straight away and older ones load as they scroll. The record Activity tab behaves the same.

## What's included

* Measure the timeline and Activity tab at full Close volume: after the 10k-call test slice, then after the full load.
* Narrow every part of the timeline query to the one person or record before joining, and add any missing index.
* Load the timeline in pages, newest first.
* Not included: the inbox list (separate tickets under ENG-14368).

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately. Measurements are most useful after the 10k-call test slice lands.

## Done when

- [ ] Opening the person with the most imported history in the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace takes under 500 ms on production.
- [ ] The timeline shows the newest 50 items first and loads older ones on scroll.
- [ ] Query plans show no workspace-wide scan for a single person or record.

## Implementation context

* AI context.md: timeline query paths, what ENG-14300 already fixed and what to measure first.

relatedSnapshot.title: Conversations stays fast as imported texts grow
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Keep Conversations fast for the AI Acquisition Sales Team as the Close text history loads. The list, opening a person and the thread pane should cost about the same however many texts the workspace holds.

## Problem

ENG-14492 made calls scale with the rows on screen. Texts still do not. After about 250k imported texts (40,586 text threads, up from 1,864), production Conversations went from about 1 s to 3 to 4 s for Everyone and about 8 s for Mine on 30 Sep. The list's text side works through every text thread in the workspace, and the thread pane reads every text message. About 190k more texts, then about 900k more in phase 2, are paused until this is fixed.

## What's included

* The list and opening a person read only the text threads of the people on screen: threads whose own contact is one of them, plus threads where a sent text is attributed to one of them.
* Opening a row with no person reads only that thread.
* The thread pane for a person reads only that person's texts.
* One small index for texts attributed to a person when sent from the app (under 1,000 rows today).
* Not included: search (tracked in ENG-14495), and the deal record page's text timeline.

## Done when

* On production, the Sales Team list, opening a person and the thread pane return in about the same time before and after the next texts batch, and their plans no longer loop once per workspace text thread.
* Results are identical before and after: old-versus-new comparison on the replica, and the ready inbox parity check reports the same mismatches for old and new code.
